title: Private deployments: VPC & On-Prem deployment guide, day-2 ops, upgrade & rollback, customer requirements library
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's canonical guidance for private deployments (VPC and on-prem). It covers: reference architectures, on-prem packaging, preflight & deployment steps, day-2 operational patterns, upgrade and rollback procedures, and a customer requirements library we use during scoping. The target audience is Solutions Engineers, SRE, Platform, and customer DevOps teams.

Scope and intent
- Scope: Production private deployments (VPC-hosted control plane with customer-managed compute, and fully on-prem air-gapped packages) for Redwood Dedicated / Private customers.
- Intent: Provide reproducible, audited procedures and checklists to reduce deployment time and minimize production incidents during day-0 and day-2.

Owner and contacts
- Primary owner: eng-private-deployments (team)
- Oncall / escalation: private-deployments-oncall@redwood.example.com
- Documentation owner: Aisha Patel (author)

Conventions used in examples
- Service names: redis-cache (prefix rwinf-redis), object-storage (S3-compatible), rwinf-runtime (GPU inference pods), rwinf-control-plane (control-plane components).
- Commands assume Linux admin host with terraform v1.5+ and kubectl/helm client tools installed.

Reference architectures

1) VPC deployment (recommended for cloud partners)
- Single-region (multi-AZ) design: 3 private subnets (control plane, runtime, infra) across AZs, dedicated NAT Gateways (or shared depending on cost), Transit Gateway for customer VPN/Direct Connect.
- Components:
  - rwinf-control-plane: runs in customer VPC private subnet (optional, customer-managed control plane for Private deployments)
  - rwinf-runtime: GPU node pool behind a private LB (NLB) with target groups per model-class
  - rwinf-data: object-storage (customer S3), kms (customer-managed CMK), redis-cache (managed or self-hosted)
- Sizing guidance (baseline per 100 RPS of 8k token workloads):
  - 4 x A100 (or equivalent) for model-serving pool (throughput depends on model family and quantization)
  - redis-cache: 4 nodes, 8GB each, replication enabled
  - object-storage: lifecycle policy, 30 days hot storage

2) On-prem reference architecture (air-gapped option)
- Rack topology: management layer (jump hosts, monitoring), control plane (HA pair), runtime racks (GPU servers), storage appliance (S3-compatible object store), optional HSM for key custody.
- Network zones: management VLAN, storage VLAN, compute VLAN, public egress (if allowed) isolated via firewall rules.
- HA patterns: control plane in active/standby with VIP, rwinf-runtime scaled across racks with local redis replica for low-latency KV caching.

Design decisions and constraints
- All deployments MUST use customer KMS for sensitive key material.
- Cross-AZ latency targets: <5ms for KV calls; if >5ms, enable local cache shards.
- Control plane telemetry should be routed to customer observability or to Redwood's ingest endpoint depending on contract (see confidentiality section).

Prerequisites and preflight checklist
- Networking:
  1. VPC CIDR planned and subnets created (control, runtime, infra).
  2. DNS hosted zone and wildcard rwinf.internal.<customer-domain> configured.
  3. BGP/VPN or Direct Connect established for private connectivity if needed.
  4. Required ports open between subnets (table below).

- IAM & crypto:
  1. KMS key ARN available and IAM role for Redwood runtime created.
  2. Service account with minimum privileges for S3/object-store operations.

- Storage & cache:
  1. Object storage bucket created with versioning and lifecycle rules.
  2. Redis or compatible cache endpoints provisioned and tested.

- Compute:
  1. GPU nodes in the pool with driver/container runtime (NVIDIA driver + containerd) validated.
  2. Node labels: rwinf/gpu=true, rwinf/zone=<zone> for auto-placement.

Preflight network port table
| Source | Destination | Protocol | Port | Purpose |
| admin-host | rwinf-control-plane | TCP | 443 | Management API |
| rwinf-runtime | redis-cache | TCP | 6379 | KV cache |
| rwinf-control-plane | object-storage | TCP | 443 | Model artifacts |
| admin-host | kube-api | TCP | 6443 | Cluster ops |

On-prem packaging and installation options

We provide two packaging options for on-prem: (A) Helm-based Kubernetes deployment (recommended where a Kubernetes cluster is available) and (B) Appliance bundle (VM images + systemd services) for non-K8s environments.

A. Helm (Kubernetes) packaging
- Artifacts: container images hosted on customer registry or Redwood registry (per contract).
- Packaging contents: Helm chart rwinf/private-deploy v{major}.{minor}, manifests for control-plane, runtime, metrics, and bootstrap jobs.
- Typical helm install command (example values inline):

helm upgrade --install rwinf-private rwinf/private-deploy \
  --namespace rwinf --create-namespace \
  --set controlPlane.replicaCount=2 \
  --set runtime.gpu.enabled=true \
  --set objectStorage.endpoint=https://s3.customer.local \
  --set kms.keyArn=arn:aws:kms:... \
  -f values.customer.yaml

Example values.customer.yaml snippet:

runtime:
  gpu:
    enabled: true
    nodeSelector:
      rwinf/gpu: "true"
controlPlane:
  replicaCount: 2
  resources:
    limits:
      cpu: "2000m"
    requests:
      cpu: "1000m"
objectStorage:
  endpoint: "https://s3.customer.local"
  bucket: "redwood-model-bucket"
kms:
  keyArn: "arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789:key/abcd-ef01"

B. Appliance bundle (non-Kubernetes)
- Contents: prebuilt VM image (Ubuntu 22.04) with init scripts, rwinf-systemd units (rwinf-control-plane.service, rwinf-runtime.service), and a local package manager to pull model artifacts from a staging server.
- Install steps (high level):
  1) Provision VM(s) per reference topology.
  2) Mount object-storage via S3FS or native client.
  3) Enable and start rwinf-systemd units: sudo systemctl enable --now rwinf-control-plane
  4) Run bootstrap: /opt/rwinf/bin/bootstrap --config /etc/rwinf/customer.yaml

Deployment procedure (VPC/Helm example)

1) Run preflight checks (scripts provided in repo):
   - ./scripts/preflight.sh --host admin-host --vars values.customer.yaml
   - Checks: DNS resolution, KMS access, S3 write/read, cluster node labels, GPU driver health.

2) Provision infra (terraform):
   - terraform init && terraform apply -var-file=vars.tfvars
   - Outputs: kubeconfig path, object-storage endpoint, redis endpoints, network IDs.

3) Install control plane (helm):
   - helm upgrade --install rwinf-control-plane rwinf/control-plane -n rwinf -f values.controlplane.yaml
   - Verify pods: kubectl get pods -n rwinf | grep control-plane

4) Install runtime pool (helm):
   - helm upgrade --install rwinf-runtime rwinf/runtime -n rwinf -f values.runtime.yaml
   - Verify nodeSelectors and GPU scheduling: kubectl describe node <gpu-node> | grep rwinf/gpu

5) Bootstrap models and artifacts:
   - /opt/rwinf/bin/model-sync --source s3://redwood-model-bucket --target /var/lib/rwinf/models
   - Check model load logs in rwinf-runtime pods.

6) Smoke test:
   - curl -sS -X POST https://rwinf.example.internal/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"input":"ping"}' | jq .
   - Expected: 200, latency < 200ms for cached prefix responses (depends on model).

7) Canary and traffic migration:
   - Use the control-plane routing APIs to create a canary route (10% traffic) to new runtime group. Monitor error rate for 30m then increase traffic.

Day-2 operations

Monitoring and alerting (recommended thresholds)
- Metrics to monitor:
  - request_latency.p50/p95/p99: target p95 < 500ms for typical generation workloads, p99 < 2s (values depend on customer SLOs)
  - model_load_time: < 30s for warm loads
  - kv_cache.miss_rate: target < 0.05
  - infra.errors.rate (>5m window): alert if >1% of requests
- Key alerts:
  - Node GPU OOM or driver crash -> P1
  - Model load failures >3 in 10m -> P1
  - Control-plane API 5xx rate >0.5% -> P1

Backups and snapshots
- Object storage (models/artifacts): daily snapshot to cold-tier; retain 30 days by default.
- Redis: enable AOF + periodic backups (daily). Confirm restore in staging quarterly.

Scaling and capacity adjustments
- Horizontal scaling for runtime: add GPU nodes to node pool and label rwinf/gpu=true; helm will pick up new nodes automatically.
- Autoscaling rules: recommend KEDA or cluster-autoscaler linked to runtime queue depth. Provide sample HPA config in appendix.

Routine maintenance
- Kernel and driver patching window: schedule quarterly maintenance, annotate expected downtime, cordon + drain nodes gracefully:
  kubectl cordon <node>
  kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=15m
  sudo apt update && sudo apt full-upgrade -y && reboot
  kubectl uncordon <node>

Upgrade and rollback procedures

Versioning policy
- Use semver for chart and runtime releases: major.minor.patch. Breaking changes only on major.
- Support matrix of model runtime vs. control-plane is maintained in our release notes.

Canary upgrade flow (recommended)
1) Create a new runtime node pool with new runtime version images (chart vX.Y.Z).
2) Deploy control-plane chart update (minor/patch) to one replica first and validate.
3) Spin up canary runtime pods and route 5-10% via routing policy for 30-60 minutes.
4) Run a defined regression test suite (smoke + evals):
   - functional tests (API correctness),
   - perf tests (latency under representative load),
   - quality checks (prompt set evals for regressions).
5) If metrics stable, incrementally increase traffic (25% -> 50% -> 100%).
6) If any critical failures, execute rollback steps immediately.

Rollback procedure (if canary fails)
1) Stop new traffic via control-plane routing API and move back to previous runtime group.
2) Scale down canary node pool: terraform/k8s scale set to 0.
3) If control-plane change caused failure and cannot be reverted via config, restore from control-plane snapshot (see below).
4) Postmortem: capture logs, alert timeline, and engineer owner.

Control-plane state snapshot and restore
- Snapshot schedule: automatic periodic snapshots of control-plane DB (etcd or managed DB) every 6 hours; retain 14 days.
- Restore steps (high level):
  - Isolate cluster and apply read-only flag to API endpoints.
  - Restore DB from snapshot: rwinf-ctl restore --snapshot /backups/ctl-2026-11-01.snap
  - Restart control-plane pods and validate state consistency.

Customer requirements library (scoping checklist)
- Security:
  - Required: KMS, private networking, RBAC audit logging, syslog/siem integration
  - Optional but common: HSM enclave, offline model signing, FIPS-compliant images
- Networking:
  - VPN/Direct Connect availability, MTU size, allowed egress hosts, proxy requirements
- Compliance & data residency:
  - Regions for data storage, retention windows, controlled access lists
- Capacity & performance:
  - Expected RPS, average tokens per request, model families to be served, latency SLOs
- Operational preferences:
  - Monitoring platform (Datadog, Prometheus+Loki, Splunk), cadence of security patching, maintenance windows

Minimum customer information required for engagement
1) Network topology and CIDR ranges
2) KMS / key management approach
3) Object-storage endpoint credentials and bucket policy
4) Expected traffic profile (RPS, tokens, concurrency)
5) Compliance constraints (HIPAA, SOC2, PCI, etc.)

Appendix A - Example terraform variables (snippet)
{
  "cluster_name": "rwinf-customer-prod",
  "region": "us-west-2",
  "gpu_instance_type": "p4d.24xlarge",
  "desired_gpu_nodes": "4",
  "kms_key_arn": "arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789:key/abcd-ef01"
}

Appendix B - Example HPA (K8s)
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: rwinf-runtime-hpa
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: rwinf-runtime
  minReplicas: 2
  maxReplicas: 20
  metrics:
  - type: Resource
    resource:
      name: cpu
      target:
        type: Utilization
        averageUtilization: 60

SLOs and operational thresholds (recommended defaults)
- Availability SLO: 99.95% per calendar month for control-plane API (adjust for Dedicated vs. Private contracts)
- Latency SLO: p95 < 500ms for small generation requests; customers serving large 8k+ contexts should define custom SLOs.
- Error budget policy: when error budget burned >50% in a 7d window, freeze non-critical upgrades and notify stakeholders.

Security and confidentiality notes
- By default this content is internal. For restricted customers mark the deployment notes as confidentiality: restricted and redact network diagrams.
- Do not ship private key material or unencrypted credentials in runbooks. Use secret stores (Vault/KMS) and reference secret URIs only.

Post-installation checklist
1) Verify control-plane and runtime health for 24h under expected traffic.
2) Confirm metrics ingestion to customer monitoring.
3) Confirm backups run and test restore windows.
4) Document operational runbook customized to customer contacts and escalation flow.

Frequently asked questions (FAQ)
Q: Can we run control-plane fully managed by Redwood in a customer VPC?
A: Yes - we offer a customer-managed VPC option where Redwood deploys control-plane components into the customer's VPC with restricted IAM role access.

Q: What is the typical delivery lead time?
A: 4-8 weeks for standard VPC deployments (depends on networking approvals, KMS setup, and model artifact availability).
